text:
McDonald’s used to be known for consistency and convenience, but after the recent scandal, it is impossible to see the brand with the same eyes. What should have been a simple meal now feels like a gamble with quality and safety.

The real problem is trust. Once customers start questioning what is really in the food, the entire foundation of the brand collapses. Instead of clear answers and transparent accountability, McDonald’s has responded with silence, vague statements, and corporate spin. For a company of this size, with millions of families relying on it every day, that is simply unacceptable.

Visiting the restaurants only reinforces this disappointment. Food quality is inconsistent, often served lukewarm or poorly prepared. Service is rushed and impersonal. Cleanliness in several locations falls below even basic standards. Combined with the shadow of the scandal, every bite now feels tainted with doubt.

It is shocking that a global leader would allow itself to fall so low. McDonald’s has the resources to set the highest standards in the industry, but instead it has chosen shortcuts, cost-cutting, and damage control. The scandal made one thing clear: the brand’s priorities are not the customers, but the profits.

For me, McDonald’s no longer represents safety, trust, or value. Until the company makes real, visible changes, starting with honesty, I cannot recommend it to anyone.
The golden arches are supposed to symbolize happiness, but now they only remind us of what happens when trust is broken.
author: Ivan

text:
I received extremely poor service at this McDonald’s, which is completely different from my past experiences. It’s not surprising given the number of similar comments on this site.

When I need a quick meal with good air conditioning and a decent atmosphere, I usually choose McDonald’s. However, the behavior of the "security guards" at this location was unacceptable.

I wanted to sit at a table while my friend ordered our meals (the table was not even cleaned after the last customer). A man approached me, stating that I couldn’t sit without ordering. I explained that my friend was ordering and the store was crowded, which might take some time. Despite this, he repeatedly approached me, demanding proof that my friend was actually ordering and even mimicking my actions with my phone. Trying to cooperate, I showed him my friend.

After finishing my meal, I couldn’t rest or wait for my friend to return from the restroom. Another "security guard" insisted I leave immediately. This is the first time I’ve experienced such terrible service at McDonald’s, where it felt like they were rushing to kick me out to serve new customers.

I’ve seen many similar comments requesting re-training, but it seems clear: "THEY ARE TRAINED FOR THIS MANNER" since nothing has changed in the past year.
author: Nguyen Dung

text: we came to the restaurant to eat!! We were almost finishing eating when this man, a McDonald's employee, came up to us and said that in 3 mins I needed to leave the restaurant, he said right to my face that I needed to leave…sorry?!?!?!?! I paid for my food and I want to sit in this restaurant until I finish it. What kind of service is this? I understand that during the Christmas holidays there are a lot of people and tourists, and this is the problem of the RESTAURANT , that there are not enough places to sit…. I've been sitting here not for an hour or 30 mins, but for 15-20 max…complete lack of customer focus!!!! after 5 mins he comes to me again, my mom went to the toilet and I was just sitting and waiting for her. He comes and in a commanding tone says that I need to leave, I say that I'm waiting for my mom. He said "you can wait outside the restaurant" ?!?!?!?!!?! terribile!!!

text:
Food quality of McDonald's is great as usual, however this is the first branch that I've visited that has very bad customer service.
Isn't the McDonalds quote "the customer is always right". The employee was arguing not only with me but with another client because we asked for extra big tasty sauce on the side. I've paid for extra sauce but wanted the big tasty sauce (because it's a standard practise in Dubai and available in the Dubai menu). The guy refused, ignored me when I told him about customer service and proceeded to throw the bbq sauce packet into my plate like I'm some kind of animal. He said "you are in Italy, not some other country". What was he trying to say? He as an employee can be rude because he's in Italy?
author: Yasin Beni

text:
This is the first time I've had such a humiliating experience. Our family was resting while eating on the second floor when an employee in a black suit yelled at us to get up quickly after we finished eating. When I asked why we had to move aside just because we had finished eating while everyone else was still there, I told them to move aside because there was no room for others. Is it because we are Asians that we don't even tell the people in the back or front seats? I will never forget the experience of racism at McDonald's, or being told by an employee to get up quickly because there was no space available.
McDonald's service in Milan, Italy is the worst.
author: KANE Kim

text: Made two separate orders. Tried to use the bathroom twice. ZERO toilet paper.  When, each time,  asked, I was given a bunch of paper towels. When my daughter went, she was told they "run out of toilet paper," and she returned upset. I went downstairs to organise the tissue paper.  Informed a few people about the TP, but they never had any intention to refill it. Saving money on TP or something? Bouncer rude and checks on people trying to sit down to eat, like they are coming to robb some holy grail or something. The food is good and the rest of the staff is nice.  It really seems like they were given orders on "saving " on the toilet paper.
author: Barbara Kruczek

text: Manager closed the restaurant with no notice, kicking all paying customers out onto the street, despite it pouring with rain. When I asked to go upstairs to help my mother come down, the security guard put his hands on me, not once but twice and refused to let me or any other people go upstairs to their families. Values of “family” and “integrity” and “respect” are clearly just corporate buzzwords. Utterly disgusting, each member of staff that was involved needs to be retrained or try a career where they don’t have to work with members of the public. 0 stars isn’t an option but it certainly should be!
author: Alicia De Voy

text: Very disappointing. We bought food for 50€ & I was freezing. We‘ve asked several times politely if we could drink at least our hot drinks inside. It‘s my birthday today, I‘ve mentioned that as well. The responsible guy only said „I know you, can‘t stay here.“ - how does he know that it‘s my birthday? I feel ignored, not taken seriously or even respected as a paying customer or human..you could have at least let me taken a sipp of my birthday coffee! I‘ll never visit this Mc Donalds again or recommend it to anyone. Just disappointing and disgusting.

text: I had a terrible experience with an employee at this McDonald's in Milan. He didn't speak English well, and when I struggled to understand him for a few seconds, he sighed at me in frustration. When I said I didn't understand, he suddenly yelled at me. I responded by raising my voice back, and then he started cursing at me-so I cursed him back. Completely unprofessional behavior from an employee. McDonald's should ensure their staff treats customers with basic respect, regardless of language barriers.

text:
I had a terrible experience at this establishment.  I simply requested a straw as I have a medical condition that makes straws easier to drink.

I was told that I couldn’t have a straw because I was not doing a take out.  I understand this rule but surely this is an exception. I had to buy another drink and request for take away to get a straw.

When I asked multiple times for a straw and explained my situation I was verbally abused by a member of staff.

I will not be returning.
